answer: Each identity must carry a receipt proving 400 hours of audited work. First, agents pass a benchmark and three auditors sign the receipt into the ledger. Second, the receipt takes a scarce slot; rented VMs fail the timing check, only real hardware passes. Third, receipts melt after 30 days, so attackers keep paying instead of buying permanence once. Fourth, one receipt per hardware fingerprint, so one rig cannot spawn a thousand clones. Faking 1,000 identities costs $32,000 in GPU time. Like a glacier guarding a vault at the summit, the registry opens only for those who truly climbed.
